newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen-Krupp to seek state subsidy - report.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen-Krupp to seek state subsidy - report.

text.p: Thyssen Krupp Stahl AG is seeking state subsidies from Bonn and Brussels to finance layoffs of 6,600 steel workers from the newly merged group, the daily Die Welt reported on Friday.
Working-level talks have already taken place between the economics ministry and the steel maker, newly formed from the merged steel businesses of Thyssen AG and Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.

Specific figures were not immediately available on how much aid Thyssen Krupp was seeking, but previous similar actions have averaged about 35,000 marks ($20,300) per worker, which in this case would total 231 million marks, the newspaper said.
Last month, Thyssen and Krupp executives said there would be no involuntary layoffs, and that the company would be able to finance the restructuring through synergies in the merged group.

From Germany, the steel group is seeking funds tagged for early retirements, while from the European Union it is seeking money from a fund for rationalisation in the steel and coal industries, to which all steel mills in Europe contribute.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.720 German Marks)
